references.text: This is the original instruction from God to Moses to make the curtain with blue, purple, and scarlet wool and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven skillfully into it.
The curtain was to hang under the hooks and separate the holy place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark of the covenant was to stand.
Describes the craftsmen whom God filled with wisdom to carry out all kinds of work, including the skilled weaving mentioned in connection with the curtain.
The curtain concealed the Most Holy Place where the atonement cover was, and Aaron could not enter behind it at any time.
The curtain in Solomon's temple was also made of blue, purple, and scarlet wool and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
The curtain represents the way into the Most Holy Place, which Jesus has opened for us as an anchor for the soul.
Behind the second curtain was the room called the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle.
The curtain represents Jesus' body, and through his flesh we have a new and living way into the Most Holy Place.
When Jesus died, the temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom, symbolizing that the way to God was now open.
Mark also tells us that the temple curtain tore in two when Jesus gave up his spirit.
Luke mentions that the temple curtain tore in two at the moment of Jesus' death.
Connects the motif of cherubim on the tent's roof directly to the curtain, showing how God's presence is integrated into the entire structure of the tabernacle.
Links the instruction for the tent's roof with cherubim directly to the making of the curtain, emphasizing the unity of God's dwelling place.
